title: Fast launch safety lanes and comms heuristics — 2026 preflight
content:
Purpose:
This is a working preflight for a short-cycle: fast launch of feature set v2026.03 with conservative safety lanes and lightweight comms. Not the full cutover playbook — focused on decisions and heuristics that let us move quickly while preserving customer SLA and observability.

Quick summary / context:
- Target release window: 2026-04-02 to 2026-04-09 (soft launch phasing).
- Scope: hosted API model switch + routing policy tweak + autoscale policy update for dedicated pools. No data-plane schema changes.
- Primary risks: unexpected latency regressions under tail load, autoscaler misconfiguration causing capacity shortage, rollout policy mismatch causing sticky sessions to old variant.

Open questions (high-priority):
- Q1: Do we need a preflight audit on KMS rotation timing? (CONF-987) — owner: Rina — answer needed by 2026-03-20.
- Q2: Are client SDK versions pinned for controlled rollout? If not, add client-side version header to ease routing. — owner: Ethan.
- Q3: Fallback model variants: default fallback (cpu-safe) vs smaller gpu variant — which has better degradation profile for latency-sensitive customers? Need perf matrix from bench (PR #1824).

Safety lane checklist (preflight):
[ ] Confirm rollback image is tagged and smoke-tested in staging (release-engineering canary tag v2026.03-rollback).
[ ] Create canary route with 1% traffic to new model variant for first 4 hours, then escalate if signals green.
[ ] Autoscaler bounds: min=3, desired=6, max=30 for dedicated pool alpha. Validate bump scripts.
[ ] Configure circuit breaker: open if 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5m OR mean latency (p95) > 1.5x baseline for 10m.
[ ] KV/prefix cache warmup script: run 24h before cutover to populate expected hot keys.
[ ] Prefix sampling rate: keep 10% for first 12h to preserve cache footprint and telemetry.
[ ] Load shed policy: graceful degrade to smaller model variant; if shedding needed, ensure telemetry tag 'degraded=true' added to responses.

Observability guardrails (what to watch):
- KPI set (baseline values captured in baseline snapshot):
  * p50/p90/p95 latency (text-gen token step), baseline: p95=145ms on hosted-prod (region us-west).
  * 5xx error rate baseline: 0.02%
  * Request throughput (RPS) baseline and tail distribution (compare to synthetic spike sims)
  * Cost per token delta (for billing rollup)
- Alerts (actionable):
  1) p95 latency increase > +30% for 10m -> pause canary escalation and notify release channel.
  2) sustained increase in retries or 403 auth failures >= 0.1% -> stop rollout and open RLSE incident.
  3) autoscaler thrash (scale up then down 3x within 15m) -> switch autoscale to manual and notify SRE.
- Dashboards to pin in the shift binder: per-route latency, token-cost trend, model-variant traffic percent, KV cache hit rate, top 25 client IDs by RPS.

Canary escalation heuristics (recommended):
- Phase A (0% -> 1%): 0–4h: watch p95/p99, 5xx, client error signals. If green, move to Phase B.
- Phase B (1% -> 10%): 4–12h: maintain sampling, run light synthetic test suite from three regions. Check cross-regional parity.
- Phase C (10% -> 50%): 12–36h: monitor user-facing errors, cost delta. If any guardrail trips, revert to previous variant with 'fast-rollback' path.
- Phase D (50% -> 100%): 36–72h: full capacity validation + final pruning of canary routes.

Communication playbook (shift-friendly):
- Pre-launch: 48h notice in #release-orchestra with quick TL;DR and links to shift binder.
- Start: send kickoff note with expected timeline, link to ops zoom + on-call roster.
- On any major alerts: page SRE -> notify #release-orchestra -> update ticket RLSE-3241 with timeline and action taken.
- Post-rollback: 1:1 with impacted customer success contacts and short postmortem (lightweight).

Mini rollout calendar (two-week view, sprint-friendly):
Week -1 (prep):
- Mon: bake rollback image, validate smoke in staging. (Owners: Release, Infra)
- Tue: run capacity sims (10–2x expected traffic), collect perf logs. (Owners: Perf)
- Wed: finalize comms drafts and on-call rotas. (Owners: Eng Ops)
- Thu: freeze non-critical infra changes. (Owners: Platform Eng)
- Fri: last-minute smoke + sign-off meeting (30m).

Week 0 (launch):
- Day 0 (Mon 04-02): 08:00 kickoff, deploy canary 1% (Phase A). Start 8-hour observation window.
- Day 1 (Tue 04-03): escalate to 10% if green. Run cross-region synthetic tests at 03:00 and 15:00 UTC.
- Day 2 (Wed 04-04): escalate to 50% if all green. Maintain special sampling and cost tagging.
- Day 3–4 (Thu–Fri 04-05/06): hold at 50% for weekend stress data capture, run nightly soak tests.
- Day 5 (Mon 04-08): escalate to 100% if no regressions; otherwise start rollback procedures.

Rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Trigger: p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 10m -> Action: immediate rollback to tagged image v2026.02, abort escalation, open RLSE incident.
- Trigger: 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> Action: reduce traffic to 0% (route back to previous variant), verify trend, follow incident playbook.
- Trigger: Autoscaler failure / OOM events -> Action: scale to safe minimal capacity, pause rollout, page infra.

Shift binder checklist (what to include in the morning shift handoff note):
- Current canary percent, observed p95/p99 deltas, top 5 clients by error rate, active incidents, list of mitigations executed.
- Links to runbooks and rollback commands (one-click where possible).
- Contact matrix: who to page for infra, model, and customer success.

Release notes (draft — for engineering and customer success to edit):
Title: Incremental model routing and autoscale improvements (v2026.03)
Short blurb: This release introduces an updated routing policy that improves tail latency under burst traffic and a refined autoscaler profile for dedicated pools. Customers should see improved consistency in request latency during short-lived spikes.
Engineering changes (high level):
- Updated routing: sticky session correction to avoid model-mismatch on retries.
- Autoscale: new cooldown and target tracking to reduce thrash on sudden load changes.
- Observability: additional telemetry tags for degraded responses and cost-per-token sampling.
Known limitations / notes to CS:
- During the initial ramp we will route a small percent of traffic to the new variant — some customers on older SDKs may see transient 429s until they pick up the header fix. We will notify affected accounts proactively.

Post-launch actions (24–72h):
- Perf: run 2x synthetic stressrun and compare against baseline.
- CS: customer outreach on high-value accounts and collect any anomaly reports.
- Infra: postmortem if rollback performed; otherwise short stabilization retro (20m).

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Might be worth adding a temporary feature-flag gate to disable the new routing per-customer quickly (fast toggle).
- Check with model-ops on best degradation label semantics — 'degraded=true' vs 'fallback_model=small-v1'.
- Validate billing metric tags so that cost-reports slice by model-variant for quick reconciliation.

Appendix: useful commands and quick links (placeholders)
- rollback CLI: rdo rollback --env prod --tag v2026.02
- promote CLI: rdo promote --env prod --canary 10
- perf sim job: perf-sim/run 2026-03-29 --scale 2x

End of doc — this is intentionally terse. We will iterate after the sign-off meeting.
